title: A closed interval of the constructive reals is Bishop-compact
statement: Bishop's definition of compactness for a metric space is COMPLETE plus TOTALLY BOUNDED -- no open sets, no covers, no finite subcover. Both halves are metric conditions and both are now stated for an arbitrary `Metric` and discharged for the closed interval `[a,b]` of the constructive reals, relativized to the predicate `Metric.Interval a b` because this kernel has no `Subtype` and a subspace here is a predicate on the ambient carrier, not a new carrier (ADR-1602). Total boundedness is the substantive half: at accuracy n the net is `g n i = CReal.min b (a + i/(n+1))` for `i <= B*(n+1)`, where B is any natural bounding `b - a` (from `CReal.archimedean`, whose `Exists` is eliminable because the conclusion is a Prop). The `min` is an obligation rather than a convenience -- `Metric.NetIn` requires every net point to satisfy the predicate, and the rational grid runs past b -- and the covering is an induction on the index bound with one `CReal.lt_cotrans` split per step. Completeness is `Metric.creal_completeOn_interval`: a Cauchy sequence inside `[a,b]` converges, and its limit is still inside `[a,b]`.

formal.statement: theorem Metric.creal_compactOn_interval : ((x0 : CReal) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> ((x2 : CReal.le x0 x1) -> Metric.CompactOn Metric.creal (Metric.Interval x0 x1))))    -- Metric.CompactOn M P := And (Metric.TotallyBoundedOn M P) (Metric.CompleteOn M P); Metric.Interval a b := fun x => And (CReal.le a x) (CReal.le x b)

evidence.supports: Metric.creal_compactOn_interval is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement, and Kernel::axiom_footprint reports 0 assumed names.
checkers: producing-build (Kernel::add_declaration, which re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example kernel_declaration_projection -- --require-declaration Metric.creal_compactOn_interval | grep -cE '^found[[:space:]]+metric[[:space:]]+theorem[[:space:]]+Metric\.creal_compactOn_interval[[:space:]]+0$'
evidence.notes: The exit status depends on the finding twice over: kernel_declaration_projection exits non-zero when the named declaration is in no constructed prelude's environment, and grep -c then exits 1 printing 0 if the anchored row is absent or its axiom-footprint column is not 0. Anchored with [[:space:]] and never \t -- in a scripted (GNU) grep \t is a literal t. grep -c rather than grep -q, which would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail. --release is MANDATORY: this binary builds creal/complex/cpoint/metric, which overflow the default debug thread stack.

evidence.supports: Every declaration of the Metric namespace, including this one and the total-boundedness theorem it rests on, has an empty Kernel::axiom_footprint. The test derives its name list from the prelude handle's three name structs and the record's own RecordNames selectors, and a companion test (every_metric_namespace_declaration_is_accounted_for) walks Kernel::environment and fails if any Metric.* declaration is missing from that list -- so the subject comes from the kernel, not from a maintainer's memory.
checkers: metric::metric_tests, run against a freshly built kernel environment
evidence.checker_command: cargo test --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib -- metric::metric_tests::every_metric_declaration_is_axiom_free metric::metric_tests::every_metric_namespace_declaration_is_accounted_for --test-threads=4 2>&1 | grep -cE '^test result: ok\. 2 passed'
evidence.notes: The `2 passed` is load-bearing: `cargo test -- <filter>` runs ZERO tests and exits 0 when a filter matches nothing, so a rename would turn this checker green while checking nothing. Requiring the exact count is what makes the exit status depend on the finding.

provenance.source: Lane `metric-compactness`, roadmap W2-3, recorded in ADR-1607 (docs/research/09-decisions/adr-1607-the-metric-layer-carries-w2-2-and-w2-3.md). formal.statement is Kernel::render_lean of the declaration's type, taken verbatim from metric_tests::w2_3_interval_types_render's printed output; axiom_footprint is read from Kernel::axiom_footprint, never from a rendered name.

notes: WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. It does not say the interval is compact in any cover sense -- no open-cover compactness is defined in this library and ADR-1602 declines to adopt one. It does not give the net as DATA: `Metric.TotallyBoundedOn` concludes with two nested `Exists`, which are Prop-valued, so a consumer cannot project out the net and compute with it; that is the same Prop-only-elimination boundary ADR-1595 measured, and it is why the EVT below is proved by eliminating those existentials inside a Prop goal rather than by building anything. It also does not say the Euclidean plane instance `Metric.cpoint` has any compact subsets -- nothing about that is proved.
